items.passage:
The knowledge which he needed he acquired quickly and soon forgot it. I do not think he ever went deeply into things in those early days, or tried to perfect himself in any sort of knowledge. He was neither generous nor acquisitive; he was ______, and always rather apt to put his little possessions away and to forget about them. It was always the present he was concerned with; he did not deal with the past nor with the future.

Then after what had been not so much a slumber of the spirit as a vivid living among immediate impressions, the artistic nature began to awake in him.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: ambitious
detached
greedy
devoted
items.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'neither generous nor acquisitive'는 그가 남에게 베풀지도, 무언가를 모으려 하지도 않았음을 말한다. 바로 뒤의 소유물을 치워 두고 잊어버렸다는 설명도 사물에 대한 무관심을 보여 준다. 따라서 '초연한, 무심한'을 뜻하는 B가 가장 적절하다. A와 D는 열정을 암시하고, C는 'acquisitive'와 같은 뜻이라 'neither … nor' 구조와 모순된다.

items.passage: While standing there a flame caught her dress; she gave a scream, dropped the flowers and ran through the door to where her father was standing in the yard. When the father saw his child coming with flame following, he ran toward her. As he ran he took off his coat and wrapping it about her face, arms and shoulders, threw her to the ground. With his left hand he kept the flame from the body, while with his right hand he fought the fire. He saved his daughter but burned his right arm to the elbow.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone shifts in the text?
options: From sudden alarm to a steady account of the father's rescue and its cost
From cheerful calm to bitter anger at the father's careless actions
From quiet grief to playful humor about the burned flowers
From tense suspense to open doubt about the father's courage
items.explanation: 지문은 불이 옷에 붙어 아이가 비명을 지르며 달려가는 급박한 장면으로 시작한다. 이후 아버지가 외투로 아이를 감싸고 불을 끄는 동작을 차분하고 구체적으로 서술하며, 딸을 구했지만 팔을 덴 대가를 밝힌다. 따라서 놀람에서 구조와 그 대가에 대한 담담한 서술로 바뀐다는 A가 정답이다. B·C·D의 분노, 유머, 의심은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Redcastle is suddenly awakened to the consciousness of loveliness that scarcely moved it to admiration two years ago, although the girl’s beauty had then the bloom and freshness of unchastened youth. Perhaps she is really lovelier now. Sorrow and passion have passed there, and left the exalted look of an awakened soul, where there was before only girlish innocence, curious and wondering about a world of which it knew nothing. She has eaten of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. The mystery of life has been revealed to her. Be sure that Eve’s beauty had a deeper meaning after she came out by the fatal gate where the angel with the flaming sword kept watch and ward.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone shifts in the text?
options: From cheerful praise of the girl to harsh criticism of her sorrow
From admiring description of the girl to reflection on how experience deepens beauty
From gloomy warning about Redcastle to lighthearted mockery of him
From confusion about the girl's looks to certainty that her beauty has faded
items.explanation: 지문은 Redcastle이 소녀의 아름다움을 새삼 깨닫는 묘사로 시작한다. 중간부터 슬픔과 열정이 '깨어난 영혼'의 표정을 남겼다고 말하고, 선악과와 이브의 비유를 들어 경험이 아름다움에 깊은 의미를 더한다고 성찰한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 비판, C의 조롱은 없고, D는 그녀가 오히려 더 아름다워졌다는 진술과 반대된다.

items.passage:
The mellow air and leaping waters of the river beyond his door were, indeed, like unto a “healing balm” to his torn and wounded heart.

The sun was high in the heavens when he turned his weary steed homeward. On his place all was in order--for that, at least, he felt grateful. The bleating of the sheep, mingling with the soft low of the cattle, told of prosperity. He returned by way of the stable, and went in to look at his racer.

“You shall run no more, my boy,” he said, lightly touching his glossy side. “Take off his halter, and turn him loose upon the pasture, but look well to him, lad, for I go away for months; and, as it fares with him, so will it with you,” and, giving the reins of his horse into the boy’s hands, he entered the house.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It opens with a horse race and then describes the crowd's reaction to it.
It presents an argument with a stable boy and then its peaceful resolution.
It follows a man's quiet ride home and ends with his parting orders about his horse.
It contrasts the man's prosperous farm with the ruin of a neighbor's land.
items.explanation: 지문은 강가의 공기가 상처 입은 마음을 달래 주었다는 문장으로 시작해 그가 집으로 말을 돌리는 장면으로 이어진다. 이어 농장이 질서 있고 번성함을 확인한 뒤 마구간에 들러 경주마에게 다시는 달리지 않을 것이라 말한다. 마지막으로 몇 달간 떠난다며 소년에게 말을 돌보라고 지시한다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, 경주 장면·말다툼·이웃과의 대조는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Though the world might taunt and sneer at the dethroned horologist, it was none the less true, as she had declared, that his hour of humiliation had been the noblest his life had known. If her heart-strings had nearly cracked with wounded pride, that brother of hers should have been brought to a confession of the sort—and she could have sobbed aloud for shame and regret far deeper seated than Otto’s own,—still he had his clear conscience. A clear conscience. Ah heaven! what a thing of joy that must be! Too blessed to dare even to think of; and she turned and busied herself in soothing down his grief, until the convulsive sobbings grew fewer and farther between, and he began to be able to collect himself.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It praises the world's judgment of Otto and then lists his past mistakes.
It describes Otto's confession in detail and then reports his punishment.
It traces the woman's grief and then explains her decision to leave Otto.
It moves from the woman's reflection on her brother to her efforts to comfort him.
items.explanation: 지문 앞부분에서 여성은 세상이 조롱하더라도 동생의 굴욕의 순간이 가장 고귀했다고 생각하며 자신의 수치와 부러움을 되새긴다. 'A clear conscience'를 되뇌는 내면 성찰이 이어진 뒤, 마지막에 그녀는 몸을 돌려 동생의 슬픔을 달래기 시작한다. 따라서 성찰에서 위로하는 행동으로 이동한다는 D가 정답이다. A는 세상의 평가를 칭찬한다고 잘못 말하고, B와 C의 처벌·떠남은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: When about seven days out, the steamer had been caught in a fog, and, going too near the treacherous coast of Newfoundland, had in the night suddenly encountered a sunken rock. __The violence of the shock aroused every one on board.__ There was a rush for the pumps, but they were of no use; the vessel already had begun to sink. Then followed a terrible scene. Men and women rushed wildly about, vainly calling for those belonging to them. Parents and their children were separated in the darkness--all, passengers and crew alike, too panic-stricken to act in concert.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It marks the moment the passengers learn of the disaster, leading into the panic.
It explains why the steamer had sailed so close to the coast in the fog.
It suggests that the crew calmly took control of the sinking ship.
It introduces a memory of an earlier voyage that ended without harm.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서는 배가 안개 속에서 암초에 부딪힌 사고가 서술된다. 밑줄 문장은 그 충격으로 모든 사람이 깨어났다고 말하며, 뒤이어 펌프로 몰려가고 사람들이 우왕좌왕하는 공포의 장면이 펼쳐진다. 따라서 승객들이 재난을 알아차리는 순간을 표시하며 혼란으로 이어 준다는 A가 정답이다. B는 앞 문장의 내용이고, C는 공황 상태와 모순되며, D의 회상은 없다.

items.passage:
Without further delay the two scrambled out through the aperture, and, creeping along the ledge, once more stood in the hollow of the ravine, at the point of its separation into the forks that had perplexed them in their ascent. __Perhaps, after all, they had chosen the right one.__ At the time of their first flight, had they succeeded in reaching the plain above, they would surely have been seen and pursued; though with superior swiftness of foot they might still have escaped.

Once more they faced upward, by the slope of the ravine yet untried.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the narrow ledge the two crept along to leave the cave.
It reconsiders an earlier choice of route, which the next sentence then supports.
It reveals that the two had been seen and chased by their pursuers.
It expresses deep regret that the two never reached the plain above.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서 두 사람은 처음 오를 때 그들을 헷갈리게 했던 갈림길로 돌아온다. 밑줄 문장은 그때의 선택이 결국 옳았을지도 모른다고 다시 생각하는 내용이다. 다음 문장은 그때 평원에 도달했다면 분명 발각되어 쫓겼을 것이라며 이 판단을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 앞 문장의 묘사이고 C와 D는 가정법 문장을 잘못 읽은 것이다.

items.passage:
I tried to think that this indifference and sunny idleness were perhaps the natural reaction of that larger life of emotion and activity from which he had just emerged. I reflected a great deal on that life, and, though I lamented the fact that he had drawn his sword on the wrong side, there was, down deep in my heart, an involuntary sympathetic throb for the valor that had not availed. I suppose the inexplicable ties of kinship had something to do with all this.

Washington Flagg had now been with us five weeks. He usually lingered awhile after dinner; sometimes spent the entire evening with the family, or, rather, with me, for Mrs. Wesley preferred the sitting-room to my den when I had company.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Washington Flagg?
options: Open contempt for his idleness and long visits
Fearful suspicion of his reasons for staying
Complete indifference to his past and company
Sympathy mixed with mild disapproval of his past
items.explanation: 서술자는 Flagg의 무관심과 게으름을 큰 감정적 삶 뒤의 자연스러운 반동이라고 이해하려 한다. 그가 '잘못된 편'에서 칼을 뽑은 것을 안타까워하면서도, 헛되이 끝난 용기에 마음속 깊이 공감한다고 밝힌다. 따라서 공감과 약간의 불찬성이 섞인 D가 정답이다. A의 경멸, B의 의심, C의 무관심은 서술자의 이해하려는 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Far less than half-way to the hamlet, very little beyond the bottom of the hill, we must come forth into the moonlight. Nor was this all, for the sound of several footsteps running came already to our ears, and as we looked back in their direction, a light tossing to and fro, and still rapidly advancing, showed that one of the new-comers carried a lantern.

"My dear," said my mother suddenly, "take the money and run on. I am going to faint."

This was certainly the end for both of us, I thought. How I cursed the cowardice of the neighbours; how I blamed my poor mother for her honesty and her greed, for her past foolhardiness and present weakness!
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his mother?
options: Exasperated blame softened by pity
Calm admiration for her courage
Cheerful confidence in her plan
Cold indifference to her fate
items.explanation: 추격자들이 다가오는 순간 어머니가 기절하겠다고 말하자 서술자는 이제 끝이라고 생각한다. 그는 어머니의 정직함과 욕심, 무모함과 나약함을 탓하지만, 동시에 'my poor mother'라고 불러 연민을 드러낸다. 따라서 연민이 섞인 짜증 어린 비난이라는 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 그의 절망과 맞지 않고, D는 감정이 강하게 드러난 문장과 모순된다.

items.passage: I was also present for one day during the races. The course is two miles in length, and in excellent condition, being railed off the whole distance. I saw one race, which was admirably contested; but the ground was not well attended, and the others did not go off with spirit. I was told, however, that there was a great prospect of improvement, as the Canadians were beginning to be fond of the sport. The excitement would have been much greater if it had lasted but two days instead of four; and a public ball afterwards would not have been amiss.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how the Canadians invented a new kind of racing
To give a mixed view of the races and suggest improvements
To complain that the racecourse was in very poor condition
To recount the narrator's own victory in a close race
items.explanation: 서술자는 경주로가 훌륭하고 한 경주는 잘 겨루어졌다고 칭찬하지만, 관중이 적고 다른 경주는 활기가 없었다고 지적한다. 이어 기간을 이틀로 줄이고 무도회를 열면 좋겠다고 제안한다. 따라서 장단점을 함께 평가하고 개선점을 제시한다는 B가 정답이다. C는 '훌륭한 상태'라는 묘사와 반대되며, A와 D는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The one selected for my riding excursions was the only saddle-horse of repute in the county; he belonged to a livery stable, and was of the “calico” red and white sort, tall, long of body, sound of legs and feet, with large, liquid, expressive eyes, small ears, and a beautiful open nostril. His pedigree was unknown, and no one in the village could say where he came from. He had been turned out lame from a “travelling show” the year before, and had been bought for a song. Such only was his brief known history. To his physical beauties were added the higher qualities of head and heart in abundance.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain how the narrator bought a horse from a show
To criticize the village for neglecting a lame horse
To introduce a horse's looks, unclear past, and character
To compare the many saddle horses found in the county
items.explanation: 지문은 서술자가 타던 말의 큰 키, 표정 있는 눈, 아름다운 콧구멍 등 외모를 자세히 묘사한다. 이어 혈통과 출신을 아무도 모르고 순회 쇼에서 절름발이로 버려졌다는 짧은 내력을 전하며, 머리와 마음의 훌륭한 자질까지 칭찬한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 말이 마구간 소유라는 진술과 어긋나고, B와 D는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: John Milton had rowed back without lifting his eyes to Mrs. Ashwood's receding figure. He believed that he was right in declining her invitation, although he had a miserable feeling that it entailed seeing her for the last time. With all that he believed was his previous experience of the affections, he was still so untutored as to be confused as to his reasons for declining, or his right to have been shocked and disappointed at her manner. It seemed to him sufficiently plain that he had offended the most perfect woman he had ever known without knowing more. The feeling he had for her was none the less powerful because, in his great simplicity, it was vague and unformulated.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “so untutored” most nearly suggests that John Milton was
options: poorly educated in his school subjects
unwilling to learn from other people
inexperienced in understanding his own feelings
too proud to admit he had made an error
items.explanation: 'untutored'는 원래 교육을 받지 못했다는 뜻이지만, 여기서는 애정 문제에 대해 쓰였다. 그는 거절한 이유나 실망할 권리에 대해 혼란스러워하고, 그녀에 대한 감정도 막연하고 정리되지 않았다고 서술된다. 따라서 자기 감정을 이해하는 데 미숙하다는 C가 정답이다. A는 문자적 의미에 머물고, B와 D의 고집이나 자존심은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: If I might see a smile on her face, if the look of yielding would but come back there and remain! Surely her scruples would pass when I should bring her father to her. What imaginary barrier could stand before the combined forces of love and gratitude? The rescue of her father must not be longer deferred. I must form my plan immediately. Yet I continued to waste time thinking of the future, of the day when she should acknowledge herself mine. I took off my hat and removed from it the glove that she had given me. It was like a part of her; it was fashioned by use to the very form of her hand.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “It was like a part of her” most nearly suggests that the glove was
options: a worn object the narrator planned to discard
a gift she had demanded that he return
a disguise that he used to hide his identity
a treasured token that seemed to hold her presence
items.explanation: 서술자는 그녀가 준 장갑을 모자에서 꺼내며 그녀의 일부 같다고 말한다. 바로 뒤에서 장갑이 사용으로 그녀 손의 모양을 그대로 띠게 되었다고 설명해 그녀의 존재가 담긴 물건임을 강조한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. 그는 미래를 꿈꾸며 장갑을 소중히 여기므로 A의 버림, B의 반환 요구, C의 변장은 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
"The city boasts an old and learned college,
Where you'd think the leading industry was Greek;
Even there the favoured instruments of knowledge
Are a driver, and a putter, and a cleek.

"All the natives and the residents are patrons
Of this royal, ancient, irritating game;
All the old men, all the young men, maids and matrons,
With this passion burn in hard and gem-like flame.

"In the morning, as the light grows strong and stronger,
You may see the players going out in shoals;
And when night forbids their playing any longer,
They will tell you how they did the different holes.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “With this passion burn in hard and gem-like flame” most nearly suggests that the townspeople
options: feel an intense and lasting enthusiasm for golf
are angry about the game's irritating rules
suffer from the summer heat on the course
pretend to enjoy golf to please their neighbors
items.explanation: 시는 대학 도시에서도 지식의 도구가 골프채일 만큼 모두가 골프를 즐긴다고 말한다. 노인과 젊은이, 처녀와 부인 모두가 이 열정으로 불탄다는 비유 뒤에 아침부터 밤까지 경기하고 홀 이야기를 늘어놓는 모습이 이어진다. 따라서 강렬하고 지속적인 열정을 뜻하는 A가 정답이다. 'irritating'은 장난스러운 표현일 뿐 분노가 아니므로 B는 틀리고, C와 D도 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Of course we all know from the books that their intention is to find a suitable spot in which to bury this ball, and such being the case, with what astonishing stupidity do they urge on that labor! Here certainly is just the right spot for you, Mrs. Tumble-bug! Stop rolling and dig! But no, she will not listen to reason. She mounts the top of the ball, and, creeping far out upon it, pulls it over forward with her back feet, while Mr. Tumble-bug helps her in a most singular fashion. Does he stand up on his hind legs on the opposite side, and push with his powerful front feet? Oh no; he stands on his head, and pushes with his hind legs. As he pushes, and as the ball rolls merrily on, Mrs. Tumble-bug is continually rolled around with it, and must needs climb backward at a lively rate to keep her place.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “she will not listen to reason” most nearly suggests that Mrs. Tumble-bug
options: cannot hear the observer over the noise of rolling
stubbornly ignores what seems sensible to the observer
is waiting for Mr. Tumble-bug to give her advice
has already found a good spot in which to dig
items.explanation: 서술자는 공을 묻을 적당한 자리를 발견하고 멈춰서 파라고 쇠똥구리에게 말을 건넨다. 그러나 쇠똥구리는 계속 공을 굴리므로, 이성에 귀 기울이지 않는다는 표현은 관찰자가 보기에 합리적인 선택을 고집스럽게 무시한다는 뜻의 의인화다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 문자 그대로의 청각으로 오해했고, C와 D는 지문 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Determined to carry to a successful completion every project we take in hand, we went to work to organize the meeting. A chairman is essential to any meeting. They are necessary to keep the meeting in order, and give the assemblage proper dignity. We were unanimously chosen chairman and took our seat amid the most profound silence. But a difficulty, wholly unexpected now presented itself. A secretary to keep the record of the proceedings is equally indispensable. There was no one to make secretary. Not to be thwarted by minor obstacles, we finally with much reluctance, consented to assume this arduous position also.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “this arduous position” most nearly suggests that the role of secretary was
options: a truly exhausting job that required long training
a post that other members fought hard to obtain
a mock-serious exaggeration of a trivial duty
a dangerous role that the narrator greatly feared
items.explanation: 서술자는 혼자서 회의를 조직하며 만장일치로 의장에 뽑혔고, 깊은 침묵 속에 자리에 앉았다고 과장된 격식으로 말한다. 서기를 맡을 사람이 없어 '마지못해' 그 자리까지 맡았다는 설명도 같은 희극적 어조다. 따라서 'arduous'는 사소한 일을 일부러 거창하게 부풀린 표현이므로 C가 정답이다. 다른 지원자가 없으므로 B는 틀리고, A와 D는 반어를 문자 그대로 읽은 것이다.

items.passage: On the ship came, and, casting anchor, several of the crew landed. They wandered about through the woods, singing and carousing, and otherwise amusing themselves. When also they happened to discover any of the cottages of the natives, they did not scruple to enter, and to ______ anything which struck their fancy. Alonzo was attending to the affairs of state when news was brought him of the behaviour of the strangers, and that they were actually approaching the precincts of the Palace. On this he immediately sent out to put a stop to the mischief. As he was proceeding a shriek reached his ear.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: return
admire
repair
appropriate
items.explanation: 선원들은 원주민의 오두막을 발견하면 거리낌 없이 들어갔다고 서술된다. 뒤이어 그들의 행동이 'mischief'로 불리고 Alonzo가 이를 막으려 사람을 보낸다. 따라서 마음에 드는 물건을 '제멋대로 가져가다'라는 D가 가장 적절하다. A와 C는 선한 행동이라 맥락과 맞지 않고, B는 저지할 만한 해악이 되지 못한다.

items.passage: I sat mending my clothes, and thinking about Captain Secretan. My thoughts were not happy ones. I was shocked to find what a hold this stranger had taken upon my mind, and how difficult it was for me to think of any one else, or to imagine my life without him. Yet I knew that he was nothing, and never could be anything to me. Poor, but proud, and of good birth, moving in what Mrs. Hazleton calls the best society, he will naturally select a woman of fortune for his wife. He is handsome, agreeable, has many gifts which distinguish him from the common run of young men, and will have no difficulty in making ______ marriage.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: an advantageous
a humble
a secret
an unhappy
items.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 그가 가난하지만 자존심이 강해 자연히 재산 있는 여자를 아내로 고를 것이라고 말한다. 또 잘생기고 재능이 많아 어려움이 없을 것이라는 설명은 유리한 결혼을 쉽게 할 수 있다는 뜻이다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 그의 장점과 맞지 않고, C는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: The cement should be made into a stiff paste, and worked into the form required. Indeed, the rockwork may be wholly composed of such cement, especially if it is to have the form of an arch. The most important matter in the construction of rockwork is to give it a natural, rugged appearance, and to avoid loading the tank with ______ weight. I have seen large shells and branches of coral in fresh-water tanks, and always thought the spectacle disgraceful to the owner. In a marine tank, such things are proper enough. Whatever is done should be made secure, the pieces of stone well embedded in cement, and the whole firmly united. The tank must be well seasoned, be frequently filled and emptied, to dissolve out any free salts before being put to use.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: necessary
superfluous
balanced
natural
items.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 바위 장식을 만들 때 자연스럽게 보이게 하고 수조에 피해야 할 무게를 싣지 말라고 말한다. 'avoid'와 함께 쓰이므로 '불필요한' 무게라는 B가 가장 적절하다. A와 C는 피할 대상이 될 수 없고, D는 앞의 'natural appearance'를 잘못 끌어온 것이다.

items.passage: Of course, I do as I would be done by. The privacy I claim for myself, I carefully ______ for others. I keep no letters of a private and passing nature. I know that others are thinking and acting with me. We enjoy, by this provision, a freedom and fulness of epistolary correspondence which could not possibly exist if the press loomed in the distance, or executors’ eyes were known to be in wait hereafter. Our correspondence has all the flow and lightness of the most secret talk. This is a present reward, and a rich one, for the effort and labour of making our views and intentions understood. But it is not our only reward. We perceive that we have fixed attention upon what is becoming an important point of Morals: and we feel, in our inmost hearts, that we have done what we could to guard from encroachment an important right, and from destruction a precious privilege.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: reveal
ignore
guard
publish
items.explanation: 앞 문장에서 서술자는 남에게 대접받고 싶은 대로 대한다고 말한다. 자신이 주장하는 사생활을 남에게도 같은 방식으로 대한다는 뜻이므로 '지켜 준다'는 C가 가장 적절하다. 이어서 사적인 편지를 보관하지 않는다는 설명도 이를 뒷받침한다. A와 D는 사생활을 침해하는 행동이고, B는 적극적 배려와 맞지 않는다.
